Homework:

This will be alot like the Read a Session Homework, except that I want you to do learn from it how to pinpoint in advance, turns in the market which will pay you very large rewards for minimal risk.

So Open a D1 chart on any pair Download as much LTF history as you can for it Start at the second price turn on the left Look to the left of it, in the lowest TF you can Work out why price reacted to that level Mark the reason on the LTF chart Take a little screenshot of that area - name it "name of pair"1 Mark the turning point on D1 with a 1 Move on to the next turning point, and repeat, and then the next. Do this for every turning point. When you're finished, you'll have a D1 chart with all the turning points numbered, and a gallery of thumbnails of the LTFs, each explaining the turns.

Do this for as many pairs as you possibly can

Believe me, it'll be well worth it!

So maybe this might help you a little bit:

What is a decision point: Well it's a price point on a chart where a decision has been made to take price either higher or lower

Where can I spot a decision point? You will see that new decision points take place at Unfresh Supply or Demand areas. Let's take a Supply area for example. New supply is created because of a new decision point. Now to take this supply away and break it, the big boys will need to make a decision and put lots of money in the market to take the supply out. So you will see that unfresh demand, eventually becomes Fresh Supply once it gets broken. This happens because all the demand was consumed (multiple retest of the area) and that there was finally a decision made to take price lower.

Hope this makes sence, if not let me know and I'll try to explain it beter. Best, Mel

Im kind of starting to collect pictures of "No-Brainer PO setups" that can be taken without waiting for PA confirmation, because the fact to get in the trade just is prior to waiting for correct PA.

So this will help me to look for very clear Price Action in the past that is still fresh and waits to be tested, especially (!) on the higher timeframes.

Here are a few examples I already have (zone of interest in orange):

Note that these setups already ocurred, these are just examples for myself to draw the orange box and set the PO at the upper line of the orange rectangle and this is how price should react and these zones MOST of the time if we draw the zones correctly.

USDCHF - facts before the trade: + Strong engulfing pattern (even on LTF) + first real retest of broken + three tap (down channel)

GBPCHF - facts before the trade: + clear rally results in a very clear H4 base with a even better break of this level + compression into the level

GBPUSD - facts before the trade: + a clear base on H1 that got broken + left the base with strong bear bars and even gapped + took out the latest rally downleg of the base arrival with no problem, indicating price was too cheap

GBPUSD - facts before the trade: + a clear resistance area on HTF that got tested several times + SFP: This is very important. Price gapped above the resistance area but closed within the resistance area with a long hammer down on daily. Lots of lots of accumulation of retail buy orders here for the sellers to go short. This is the best scenario at strong areas to cause major reversals. If you search for this "failed-to-break" and "stay-in-the-zone" pattern with a clear bar on the HTF, you will find awesome trading opportunities.

GBPJPY - facts before the trade: + it was a very bullish uptrend during the time this trade happened, so looking for LONG POs + price kind of made a small resistance and broke this level big style with a move just over 300 pips + we even had a clear smaller TF base that got broken by an engulfing bar, so this is the area of interest for the PO. decisions. The realization already is that price is only ever moving from one decision point to another, and the invariant at any decision point (DP) is value. If price falls away from an area, its decided price is too expensive - this is the invariant at this level at this moment. The basis to that invariant is the amount of supply that such a DP attracts. After the decision is made, different market participants may then join in, not until, adding more supply and helping the invariant hold when price returns - RTM style trading does exactly that.

v=ov9kH54Z-

dM

The core move that we see is a move up into a space we can reason about, which is, if upwards, an DP area where it was previously decided price was too expensive. There will probably be resting limit orders, as well as active traders watching as price returns to the area. Everyone is waiting for some confluence depending on their trading modality, but at some point the supply/demand invariant holds or it breaks. So the move up happens, and the sign that price is too expensive is the engulf down. Some engulfs matter more than others it seems, and if a key DP is engulfed, price ascends in the winds of demand that it consumed, until those winds fade out and price returns to that last place where supply was overwhelming. This is the FTB trade down. And of course, the key to the DP is how the decision was made - was it timid, or was there conviction.

But the primary takeaway is that price is bouncing between decisions on value. One cannot say that its just some invariant that holds until price at a certain level in the book hits zero, because it is dropping as well as rising as the dynamics of the decisions about value play out.

Harry's comment that I posted ended up in my journal because I was confused, so take heart because you are not alone. My (less than) 2 cents worth and suggestions for you: 1. Like Lupy said, treat this like an interest you're investigating right now, as if it were mountain biking, knitting, or photography, but DO NOT worry about what you do or do not understand right now or who is or is not making money - you wouldn't be worried about every detail, method, or maneuver if you were thinking about taking up biking, knitting, or photos, so the same applies here. 2. Forget terminology for now and just think of it this way: price can only go up or down, right? (It never truly goes sideways, so forget that for now.) Yes, price goes up or down. Before it goes up or down, the market makes a decision and that decision is what sends it up or down. Do not allow yourself to complicate it with terms for now! If price went up, the market made a decision. And if price went down, the market made the opposite decision. Nothing more, nothing less. 3. Perhaps you think I'm oversimplifying. OK, then disregard everything that I've said and watch this videoby If and read and reread the following words as many times as necessary until you believe it: "... decisions, that's all supply and demand is and that's all that support and resistance are. It's just decisions on the value of an asset." ~ Ifmyante in the video linked above 4. Once you've heard, read, and watched the video in #3 enough times to believe it like you believe the sun is hot, look at the charts below and keep everything simple and see if you follow as I try to "Find the Decisions" as this thread's title says. I'm trying to A. find an engulf; then B. mark where I think the decision was made to create that engulf; then C. watch what happens the first time back to the price where the decision was made. ABC - we've got this!

Post your questions, find the ABC's on your charts and know that the RTM community stands ready to help you learn but please: don't give up!

There are decisions all over the chart - it does not make them tradeable or qualifies as a system.

Flips, fresh S/D. FL's, QM's, FTRs. tips of CP etc etc - yes, you will always find a reason why price turns (just keep looking left - a bit further, further...). Again, it still does not mean you will be consistently profitable identifying them.

Sometimes the decision will appear on a 1M and sometimes it will be "obvious" on a daily. Sometimes the "decision" will be 50 pips apart dependent upon the timeframe. Again - good luck making money with it. But after the event - you will look like a genius

FTB to a DP with CP on approach - yes - sounds good, but watch how many fail.

Suddenly, you realise this is a game of probabilities as much as this site and others seem to promote something far more certain. Suddenly you realise RR, trade management, HTF context, time of day, volatility, account size and other variables are much more important than this site and most give credit to.

Everyone can keep getting excited when price turns to the pip, because on a 1M there was a flip zone, but I guarantee you - it will just continue to perpetuate the retailer dream.

Just because anyone keeps posting pip precise trades (after the event of course) that just never lose, please accept that they are not showing their losers.

Of course there are many that do not have the experience to appreciate this reality and will dismiss this post, thinking I am just another frustrated losing trader. Maybe I am, maybe I am not.

But for all the losing traders here, I dare you to come back in 2 years and read this post again and tell me I am wrong.

This post is in no way directed to polymorph, and I am not suggesting that finding decisions is not part of the process, but the fascination with pip perfect entries will ultimately distract you from the real objective which is to consistently make $.

I love trading and really respect both new and experienced traders for having a go in the market, but eventually the insanity has to stop.

GL all.

Hi Nytewyre,. I noticed you sometimes marked the decision to break which is the base just before a barrier like S/R. I am giving you this information because I wasted so much time on conventional S/D trading which teaches these areas are true supply and demand. Erase that from your mind. You will even see how RTM has changed over time. What makes this place great is the fact that even IF and other Masters never sit idle with how they see the market. They adapt. You will love it here!!!

The true DPs occur seconds after the barrier is broken and it retraces. Its often hidden in the tick chart and makes for a great trap for those S/D traders who swear by peaks and valleys as true supply/demand. The less visible our DP kink the better, especially if it retraces and forms a high/low which makes for a great FO zone.
